# Penny Royal — Qwen3.8 on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell

> SGLang-derived runtime for long-context local agents on one or two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs: Flash-Next NVFP4 with native NEXTN MTP and FR-Spec — with optional DFlash2 on a separate draft model — or Qwen3.8-27B FP8 with DFlash2.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000
Display name: Penny Royal. CLI, API model name, paths and package identifiers
keep the existing `pennyroyal` spelling.

Penny Royal 3.1 keeps
the native NEXTN MTP Flash-Next profiles as the maintained default with
unchanged recipes and widths fixed by active concurrency (block 8 for one
running request, block 4 for two or more), and adds Flash-Next DFlash2 as an
optional profile: the
existing OrcaRouter ModelOpt NVFP4
target with the separate `incoai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-DFlash2` draft, FR-Spec on
the bundled 65,536-ID map, and verification widths fixed by active concurrency —
block 6 for one running request, block 4 for two or more. Accepted draft tokens
verify through FlashInfer's SM120 kernels (`--linear-attn-verify-backend
flashinfer`, fixed in the recipes; earlier candidates verified through the
Triton path). Automatic KV pool
sizing replaces the preset cap; an explicit `MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS` override remains.
The 27B FP8 DFlash2 profile
is unchanged at fixed block 8. Native width routing ships as the bundled
tiered policy (block 8 at one running request, block 4 at two or more);
since 3.1.2 the policy is selectable with `PENNY_MTP_POLICY` and `tiered`
remains the default. The prepared release is Penny Royal 3.1.4, one Anthropic
fix awaiting publication: histories carrying recognized nested
`tool_reference` blocks that returned HTTP 500 on the bundled Froggeric v22.5
template now render safely, preserving names, order and IDs, keeping native
structured handling where supported, with unsupported blocks still returning a
clean HTTP 400, the chat template unchanged and no default, setting or sampling
movement (issue #137, PR #138, reported by @BoneGoat). Until that tag and image
publish, the current release is Penny Royal 3.1.3, six accepted
correctness fixes over the 3.1.2 source: Anthropic thinking accepted without a
`budget_tokens` figure (#124), an explicit `reasoning.effort` on the Responses
API outranking the launch default, incomplete NIXL file-backed restores refused
instead of trusted (#122), QSA retained prefix keys in narrow speculative
windows (#123), truncated hybrid-Mamba prefill chunks ending on a KV page
boundary (#109), and admission no longer staying shut on an already-empty
running batch (#126, selected part; the ownership and capacity work is not
included). It also
corrects one maturity label: **27B + DFlash2 is established and qualified**, and
only the optional Flash-Next `next-dflash2` profile stays experimental / alpha.
The draft's additional host cache is documented on both DFlash2 profiles and is
not reduced by this release. All seven pull requests are merged (#127-#132 for
the fixes, #133 for the maturity correction and release records), with
documentation followups #134 and #135 merged on top. The release tag
`pennyroyal-v3.1.3` is published at
https://github.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/releases/tag/pennyroyal-v3.1.3
and the image is published as `ghcr.io/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000:v3.1.3`,
digest `sha256:cdba5f8d72098813454aa552bad35873d65b2ba8cd72f93f3ae3ed7057c0636a`,
built (run
https://github.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/actions/runs/40525831339) from
`ec1f64e850f31f33decee6d925ab2d57a52341c3` and promoted without rebuilding (run
https://github.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/actions/runs/40549616706), as
recorded in release-3.1.3.json. The published image was checked with GPUs hidden
and no network and passed a quick actual-GPU serving smoke on the Flash-Next
profile with the public `tiered` default on October 27, 2026; that is image
serving evidence, not a new throughput qualification. The
3.1.1 NVMe PLE source-gate
removal stays in effect, the 3.1.2 width-policy setting and checkpoint-tracking
fix stay in effect, and the 3.1 feature details, source identity,
checked image digest and build remain in release-3.1.json and RESULTS.md.

## Hardware and profiles

The inference target is RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), TP1 or TP2. TP2 is
part of the DFlash2 capability: it is expected to work; it has not been tested
on two-GPU hardware. Ampere and Ada Lovelace are retained in the narrowed build for optional sidecar image preprocessing, not as
alternative inference targets. CPU image processing is also available. Local
performance measurements use TP1; community TP2 measurements are attributed
separately.

Both profiles support 524288-token context, tools, reasoning, images, RAM
HiCache and optional NIXL disk caching. NIXL is on by default; disabling it
preserves GPU/RAM caching. NVMe PLE is an independent placement choice.

Flash-Next DFlash2: `.95` static memory fraction for image-workload headroom,
6 requests / 36 Mamba slots, 2,048-token draft window, 32 decimal GB HiCache,
NIXL enabled, FR-Spec with full target verification, the resident rowwise-FP8
output head shared with the target, and draft GPU KV bounded to the sliding
window while ordinary host HiCache capacity is preserved. The widths come from
`configs/pennyroyal/adaptive-dflash2.json`, one candidate per tier, so the
3.0-era `SPECULATIVE_NUM_DRAFT_TOKENS` setting is retired on this profile.
27B DFlash2: unchanged FP8 target and draft, fixed block 8, `.92`,
4 requests / 24 slots, 96 decimal GB HiCache. 27B + DFlash2 is the established
and qualified 27B path and carries no alpha label; only Flash-Next + DFlash2
(`next-dflash2`) is experimental / alpha. The draft's own host cache is extra to
the HiCache figure on both DFlash2 profiles - the recorded 27B launch spent
79.45 GB of target KV plus 16.63 GB of Mamba state and a further 24.83 GB of
draft sliding-window cache, about 120.91 GB of caches before other process
memory - documented, not reduced. C is request concurrency,
independently of the TP GPU count.

## Installation

The baseline paths are native source installation or a prebuilt container
with ordinary host run/configuration files. Configuration lives outside the
image: run.sh selects the image/devices/mounts; the host startup directory is
mounted read-only at /config and executed there. Models and writable caches
have separate mounts. Edit host files and restart to change settings; keep
them when upgrading the image. No image rebuild or Compose setup is required.
End users never build an image.

The beta configurator is optional. It writes new timestamped files and prints
the exact launch/check commands. Existing saved files remain unchanged. Follow
the generated paths rather than assuming the default file was overwritten.

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/pennyroyal-main-sm120-final/README.md): Overview, model choices, current results and setup links.
- [Container](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/pennyroyal-main-sm120-final/docker/pennyroyal/README.md): Prebuilt image, external startup files, GPU visibility and mounts.
- [Native build](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/pennyroyal-main-sm120-final/BUILD.md): Install or upgrade the runtime and its dependencies.
- [Native launch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/pennyroyal-main-sm120-final/RUN.md): Model/cache paths, startup, TP selection and API checks.
- [Configuration reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/pennyroyal-main-sm120-final/CONFIGURATION.md): Every supported setting, default, override, interaction and restart/cache effect.
- [Beta configurator](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/pennyroyal-main-sm120-final/CONFIGURE.md): Optional setup assistant and saved-file behavior.

## Performance and release details

Use SGLang's native reported generation throughput for headline tok/s. Mean is
elapsed-time weighted over complete active decode intervals; peak is the
highest native sample from the same window. Include reasoning. Exclude the
first idle/prefill-crossing interval and partial boundaries consistently.
Client wall time and kernel-only timing are separate metrics. C4/C6 figures
are aggregate, not per-request rates. Use normal non-greedy sampling and record
the actual reasoning settings. A synthetic agent transcript is not a real
tool workflow.

Current Flash-Next results on one RTX PRO 6000. The maintained native-MTP
default, measured October 21, 2026 on the merged final source (`fe5f02c`) at
its routed widths, recorded 197.87 tok/s mean / 345.30 sampled peak for a
single request at block 8, 555.11 / 731.06 aggregate at full C4 and 472.79 /
528.49 aggregate at full C6 with block 4, a real coding workflow at 252.83 /
501.63 and the completed ten-slide presentation workflow (agentic, explicit
medium) at 216.23 / 525.80 with 80 model turns and 133,430 output tokens. On
the optional DFlash2 profile with FlashInfer verification (final candidate
source `a60f442`), a single request at block 6 recorded 241.49 / 339.53, the
full six-request batch at block 4 recorded 504.80 / 568.90 aggregate, and the
completed ten-slide presentation workflow (agentic, explicit medium) recorded
217.19 / 448.70 with 70 model turns and 132,873 output tokens. The earlier
native C1 screen at `a60f442` (227.54 / 375.90) remains dated evidence.
Dated earlier 3.1 screens on the Triton
verification path remain in RESULTS.md: the five-slide xhigh presentation
194.56 / 421.35, the coding flow 235.60 / 417.50 (`5ca3f39`), the normal
single request 228.44 / 336.20, and the fixed-W4 screens 214.18 / 306.44 and
566.14 / 657.52. A medium-effort coding rerun did not complete and is not an
accepted published benchmark. Current 27B results at fixed W8 (`27f9eaa`): 133.06
/ 232.07 single request, 459.74 / 570.73 full four-request aggregate. Each row
keeps its recorded source, profile and width label; see RESULTS.md for the
exact conditions.

Newer dated rows for the 3.1.3 candidate (`ef3258749b`, October 27, 2026, one
RTX PRO 6000 TP1, 524,288-token context) are in RESULTS.md: Flash-Next native
MTP with the locally selected `adaptive` policy at xhigh, 209.75 / 299.44 at C1
(127 intervals), 510.02 / 691.71 full-C4 aggregate (188) and 461.90 / 572.34
full-C6 aggregate (111) at 6 requests / 36 Mamba slots with 32 decimal GB
HiCache; and 27B DFlash2 at fixed W8, xhigh, 4 requests / 24 slots, 96 decimal GB
HiCache, FP32 Mamba state and a 1,466,304-token automatically sized pool, 116.99
/ 205.02 at C1 (128) and 404.3877 / 538.55 full-C4 aggregate (135 intervals over
159.876 eligible seconds). Cold-prompt time to first token on those launches: 4.50
s / 59.05 s (Flash-Next) and 10.61 s / 296.77 s (27B) at 63,906 and 489,921
tokens. The public width-policy default is still `tiered`, so the Flash-Next rows
are not a matched comparison with the October 21 screens and no speed-up is
claimed; the 27B run's 201.86-second client batch wall time is a separate
end-to-end metric, not a native decode rate.

The reasoning suite scored 93.46/100 (Flash-Next, recorded on the DFlash2
qualification) and 96.94/100 (27B) with
actual answer grading on the qualified sources; extended or repetitive
reasoning is not penalized and `ask_user` is a valid tool choice. Recorded
deviations are listed with the measurements.

Penny Royal did almost all the coding for these releases, including ports and
integration; John, Penny and Codex worked through the architecture, tuning,
verification-backend choice and debugging together. Direct Penny contributors for 3.1: @jhsmith409 and
@LocalhostRonin.
